correctness.rationale: For each nonroot edge the extinction event is that all descendant tips are extinct; independent and common-shock probabilities are \(q^s\) and q, so linearity gives Delta=theta((n-2)q-sum \(q^s\)). Exhaustively enumerating six rooted binary shapes by root partitions yields the six four-term clade polynomials. Each of the five consecutive polynomial gaps factors into positive powers of q and 1-q on (0,1). E and F have exactly two leaves at depth 2 and four at depth 3 and differ in clade sum by \(q^2(1-q)^2\). The fringe graft changes no outside descendant size and therefore changes Delta by exactly -theta \(q^2(1-q)^2\). The accompanying standard-library verifier independently generated six shapes and checked all 64 extinction subsets over 72 shape/parameter combinations with exact rational arithmetic; this corroborates but is not relied on for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is neither the previously established qualitative greater loss from correlated extinction nor the previously known existence of two six-tip Sackin-minimal trees. It is a complete strictly ordered six-topology extinction-excess comparison for a precisely specified exchangeable catastrophe model, a factored separation of the two equal-depth topologies, and a local improvement that works within arbitrarily large trees. Full relevant text of Faller and Steel and Fischer was compared by objective and implication; a directly relevant 2018 ranked-tree paper could only be compared at abstract level and remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: A highly relevant 2018 ranked-tree extinction full text was inaccessible; no claim of a whole-document exclusion is made.
Potential generic rooted-clade functional extremal results or earlier exact enumerations might imply this specific six-tip ranking even without identical language.
Bibliographic searches and a local record comparison cannot prove global novelty or independent scientific validation.

value.rationale: Correlated extinction can destroy clades as units; expected phylogenetic diversity loss is an established conservation objective. The exact first six-tip ordering identifies the two distinct equal-Sackin-balance arrangements and their universally strict penalty difference, not an arbitrary numerical tree slice. The depth-preserving six-fringe graft propagates the invariant distinction to trees of unrestricted size, demonstrating a general structural inadequacy of leaf depth as an extinction-risk proxy while keeping the species level depths fixed. It is a motivated mathematical boundary and a reusable local improvement; it does not assert empirical policy benefit.
